header: The omnibar's employee questions now go through the language model, which writes the read-only SQL. Order of events for a question typed in the omnibar (semantic mode):
1. Holiday questions that the existing deterministic holiday parser recognises are answered by it, exactly as before (a separate, verified feature; it is not a filter on employee questions).
2. EVERYTHING else is handed to the model, with no keyword gate. The model decides:
- an employee question -> SQL -> answer (count / people cards / table), with "Understood as", the SQL, the departments covered and a tick/cross;
- not about employees (circulars, policies ...) -> the app falls through to circular search;
- about employees but needs data we do not hold (salary ...) -> a plain explanation;

3. Safety net: if the model path is unavailable (provider limit or outage) or cannot produce a working query, the previous rule-based employee engine answers instead, so I never let the omnibar go dark.
Kill switch: NL2SQL_OMNIBAR_ENABLED=false sends employee questions to the previous engine only.

symbols.name: RetryInfo
doc: Describes a "No" on an earlier answer, which asks for another attempt.

members.name: logId
doc: The nl2sql_log row of the rejected answer; null when it was not model-written (holiday, old engine, circular).

members.name: attempt
doc: The attempt number of the answer that was rejected (1 = the first answer).

symbols.name: parseRetry
symbols.sig: export function parseRetry(sp: URLSearchParams): RetryInfo | null
doc: I read a retry request from the search URL: ra = attempt number of the rejected answer (if ra is present, it means "this is a retry"), rl = its nl2sql_log id, rr = the reason code, rn = the person's own words.

symbols.name: MAX_ATTEMPTS
symbols.sig: const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
doc: My limit: after this many attempts the system stops and records the case for review.

members.name: holiday
doc: Returns the existing deterministic holiday answer, or null when the question is not a holiday question.

members.name: hospital
doc: Handles a question about the hospital OPD (days, doctors, open or closed, timings). I answer it from the hospital data with no model call (step 51a); null when the question is not about it. Optional, so older callers need nothing.

members.name: pax
doc: Handles a question about the PAX directory (step 63a): the land-line numbers of the departments and places. I read them from public.pax_directory with the application's OWN connection, never the model's read-only client and never the nlq schema; null when the question is not a PAX question. Optional, so older callers need nothing.

members.name: employeeAdmin
members.type: (q: string, ticket: string | null) => Promise<AnalyticsPayload | null>
doc: Handles a request to CHANGE employee data (step 66a). The HOD of C&IT, and an executive he has authorised, get the employee manager; everybody else, logged in or not, gets one plain sentence. Returns null when the sentence is not such a request.

members.name: dates
members.type: (q: string, ticket: string | null) => Promise<AnalyticsPayload | null>
doc: Gives the date of birth or date of joining of an employee (step 65b): ONLY the HOD of C&IT may know them. He gets an answer; everybody else, logged in or not, gets one plain sentence; null when the sentence is not about an employee. The person is the LOGIN's ticket (`userKey`), never anything typed. Optional, so older callers need nothing.

members.name: cugPattern
members.type: (q: string, ticket: string | null) => Promise<AnalyticsPayload | null>
doc: Handles a question about the FIRST DIGITS of executives' CUG numbers ("executives whose CUG number does not start with 943479"). I read it by rules and answer it with the application's own code for a signed-in executive, never with the model (src/lib/contact/cugPattern.ts); null when the sentence is not such a question.

members.name: paxAdmin
members.type: (q: string, ticket: string | null) => Promise<AnalyticsPayload | null>
doc: Handles a request to CHANGE the PAX directory (step 64a): "add new pax number", "delete pax 42046", "delegate pax to ...". The editor opens for the HOD C&IT and for an executive he authorised; for anybody else a plain message says why not. The person is the login's ticket (`userKey`), never anything typed. Optional, so older callers need nothing.

members.name: holidayAdmin
members.type: (q: string, ticket: string | null) => Promise<AnalyticsPayload | null>
doc: Handles a request to manage HOLIDAYS: "manage holidays", "holiday admin", "seed holiday", "clear holiday".

members.name: circularAdmin
members.type: (q: string, ticket: string | null) => Promise<AnalyticsPayload | null>
doc: Handles a request to manage CIRCULARS: "circular management", "post circular", "upload circular", "new circular".

members.name: announcementAdmin
members.type: (q: string, ticket: string | null) => Promise<AnalyticsPayload | null>
doc: Handles a request to manage ANNOUNCEMENTS: "announcement management", "post announcement", "publish announcement", "announcement admin".

members.name: accessLogAdmin
members.type: (q: string, ticket: string | null) => Promise<AnalyticsPayload | null>
doc: Handles a request to view or manage the CONTACT ACCESS LOG: "access log management", "contact access log admin", "access log".

members.name: managementHub
members.type: (q: string, ticket: string | null) => Promise<AnalyticsPayload | null>
doc: Handles the MANAGEMENT PAGE ("management", "admin"): it lists the titles of the management tools this person may open. It asks nobody for anything unless the sentence IS such a request; someone not signed in, or without authority, gets one plain sentence.

members.name: legacy
doc: The previous rule-based employee engine, kept as my safety net.

members.name: verifiedMin
doc: How many different people must confirm an answer before I serve it without the model.

members.name: skipModel
doc: Front-path gate (src/lib/search/frontGate.ts): the question cannot be an employee question, so I skip the model (and the old engine) and let the app continue with circular search. The holiday parser and verified answers still go first.

members.name: phdTickets
doc: The tickets of the PhD holders (employees/honorific.ts DR_TICKETS when absent); the tests give their own (step 56b).

members.name: scope
doc: The FIXED SELECTION the reader made (src/records/scope.ts). "auto" (the default) lets every path run as before; a chosen one runs only its own paths, with the line made its own by the domain's cue word.

symbols.name: peopleFor
symbols.sig: export async function peopleFor(client: SqlClient, tickets: string[]): Promise<EmployeeResult[]>
doc: The omnibar's people cards need more than the four columns the model selects (P.No, contact flags, the executive badge, the id used by the masked "reveal" button), so I look them up here, by ticket number, in the order the model's SQL returned them (its seniority order). Contact values are masked exactly as the existing search masks them; the real values still come only through the existing reveal endpoint. This runs with the application's normal database role, not the model's read-only one.

symbols.sig: export async function runRosterFinder(input: FinderInput, userKey: string | null, deps: Pick<OmnibarDeps, "withClient">): Promise<OmnibarPayload>
doc: THE DEPARTMENT & DESIGNATION FINDER (src/lib/nl2sql/rosterFinder.ts): the reader picked a department and/or a designation, so the list is a fixed SQL template with no model call. It takes the SAME road as a model-written answer from the guard onward (the read-only executor, the log row, the people cards, the masking at the route's boundary, "Show more" paging), so it behaves like every other list of people.

symbols.name: adminResponders
symbols.sig: function adminResponders(): Pick<OmnibarDeps, "managementHub" | "employeeAdmin" | "paxAdmin" | "holidayAdmin" | "circularAdmin" | "announcementAdmin" | "accessLogAdmin">
doc: THE MANAGEMENT REQUESTS, in one place: the management page ("management", "admin") and the six management tools' own requests (employee, PAX directory, holiday, circular, announcement, contact access log). Each reads the sentence first (pure) and asks the database who is asking only for a sentence that IS its request. The search route tries them FIRST (answerAdminFast below), before anything slow: the name checks and the language-model router would otherwise make a page that is only a list wait for them. The chain still has them too, for a request that got past the early try (a retry).

symbols.name: answerAdminFast
symbols.sig: export async function answerAdminFast(q: string, userKey: string | null): Promise<OmnibarPayload | null>
doc: Answers the management page, or one of the tools' own requests, at once (null for any other sentence): the first of them that reads the sentence as its own wins, in the same order as in the chain.

symbols.name: answerOmnibar
symbols.sig: export async function answerOmnibar(q: string, userKey: string | null, retry: RetryInfo | null = null, opts: { skipModel?: boolean; scope?: ScopeId } = {}): Promise<OmnibarPayload | null>
doc: This is the entry point used by the search route: it wires the real model, database and existing engines.
